reports.title: Central Statistical Organization (CSO) institutional core
reports.description: Primary national statistical office responsible for censuses, surveys, national accounts, prices, labour, demographic and multi-domain socio-economic statistics. Publishes the Statistical Yearbook and participates in the IMF enhanced General Data Dissemination System (e-GDDS).
reports._notes: Foundational institutional node for the Myanmar statistical system. Data continuity and coverage are constrained relative to many peers.
reports._cadence_evidence: CSO site advertises the Myanmar Statistical Yearbook as its flagship, latest edition 2025, one per year. The site also lists Selected Monthly Economic Indicators (monthly) and a Quarterly Statistics Bulletin, but the newest SMEI shown is January 2021 and the newest quarterly bulletin is 2022-2023, so only the annual yearbook is still current; 1 reflects the yearbook.

reports.title: Population census and estimates
reports.description: Official population census and subsequent estimates. Population is approximately 55 million; the age structure remains relatively young.
reports._url_evidence: MMSIS (Central Statistical Organization) 'Census Reports' page listing the 2014 Myanmar Population and Housing Census volumes (Union Report Vol 2-B/2-C, thematic reports on mortality, gender, disability, older population) and the 2014-2050 population projections report.
reports._cadence_evidence: MMSIS population file list shows only 2014 census thematic outputs (e.g. thematic report on population projections 2014-2050), all with the same entry date of 2018-03-22. No periodicity is stated and there is no second census cycle on the page to count from.

reports.title: National Accounts of Myanmar (GDP)
reports.description: Official national accounts (GDP). Central macro-output series for an economy heavily shaped by agriculture, extractives, informal activity and political-institutional constraints.
reports._notes: Primary macroeconomic output node. Interpretation requires care given data gaps and informal activity.
reports._url_evidence: MMSIS 'National income' indicator page for Gross Domestic Product (At Current Producers' Prices), showing a 2012-2023 series in Kyat million (125,338,951.9 for 2022) broken into agriculture, industry and services.
reports._cadence_evidence: MMSIS GDP indicator is a single annual series (GDP at current producers' prices by sector) with one observation per year from 2012 to 2023; no sub-annual periods and no stated update frequency. Series is effectively dormant - it ends at 2023 with no later period posted.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index and inflation statistics
reports.description: CPI and inflation rates. Inflation has been elevated and volatile in recent years under exchange-rate pressures and supply disruptions.
reports._notes: Core high-frequency price node under elevated-inflation conditions.
reports._url_evidence: MMSIS/CSO 'Inflation Reports' series page listing monthly inflation report PDFs; note the series visibly stops at December 2020, so it is a dormant post-coup product page rather than a current one.
reports._cadence_evidence: MMSIS CPI file list is a run of monthly 'Inflation Report (Month Year)' items - March 2020 through December 2020 on the first page, with further pages of earlier months. Series is dormant: the newest edition is December 2020, so nothing has been posted for five years, but the cadence while running was monthly.

reports.title: Balance of Payments and external accounts
reports.description: BOP and external-sector statistics. Current-account dynamics, limited FDI, and large errors and omissions reflecting informal and unrecorded cross-border activity are recurring features.
reports._notes: External-accounts node under constrained data and institutional conditions.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved and read: Myanmar Statistical Yearbook 2024, Part 3 (Central Statistical Organization). It contains Chapter 13 'Foreign Trade and Investment', whose Table 13.15 is 'Balance of Payments' for FY2019/2020 to FY2023/2024, with current-account items (exports f.o.b., imports f.o.b., trade balance, services, primary income, secondary income) and financial-account components. This is an official national BOP presentation, obtained after the NSDP's designated URL (cbm.gov.mm/content/3905) again failed - cbm.gov.mm returns HTTP 503 on robots.txt for both www and bare hostnames.
reports._url_route: successor publisher - CSO publications index (csostat.gov.mm) after the NSDP-designated CBM page stayed unreachable
reports._cadence_evidence: The linked file is Myanmar Statistical Yearbook 2024 Part 3 (foreign trade and investment chapter); the yearbook is an annual CSO volume and its methodology sheets give dissemination frequency as 'Yearly' for these tables.

reports.title: Agriculture production statistics
reports.description: Official and compiled statistics on crop and livestock production. Agriculture remains a large share of employment and rural livelihoods; rice is the dominant staple and a material export crop.
reports._notes: Core primary-sector production node. Data coverage is incomplete relative to pre-2021 benchmarks.
reports._url_evidence: MMSIS/CSO 'General Reports' page whose listing is dominated by the Myanmar Agricultural Statistics series, most recent edition covering 2016-2017 to 2024-2025.
reports._cadence_evidence: MMSIS lists successive editions of Myanmar Agricultural Statistics, each covering a rolling set of fiscal years - 2012-13 to 2020-21 (entered 2023-01-03), 2013-14 to 2021-22 (2023-04-28), 2014-15 to 2022-23 (2024-03-22), and two newer volumes entered 2026-06-19. Roughly one new edition per year; no explicit frequency statement.

reports.title: Rice production and area statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from CSO and remote-sensing / agricultural monitoring sources
reports.description: Statistics and estimates on rice cultivation area and production. Ayeyarwady and other delta/lowland regions are central; production levels interact with climate, conflict and input constraints.
reports._notes: Foundational food-security crop node under constrained conditions.
reports._url_evidence: FAO GIEWS Country Brief for Myanmar (dated 20 Feb 2026) forecasting aggregate paddy production at 27.9 million tonnes and describing sowings versus the 2020-2024 average; area figures are not given.
reports._cadence_evidence: FAO GIEWS Country Brief for Myanmar carries only 'Reference Date: 20-February-2026' and an unindexed Archives link. The page states no update cycle and shows no countable list of dated prior briefs, only scattered special reports (2019, 2016, 2009).

reports.title: Natural gas production and export statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from trade and energy sources
reports.description: Statistics on natural gas production and exports. Petroleum gas is among Myanmar’s largest export commodities by value; primary destinations include Thailand and China.
reports._url_evidence: IEA country page for Myanmar's natural gas sector; the page is confirmed to be Myanmar's natural gas section (supply, production, imports/exports framing) but the underlying figures load from the IEA data browser and were not visible in the fetched text - weakest confirmation in this set. No Myanmar government gas statistics exist online: MOEE/MOEP publishes electricity only and MOGE has no site.
reports._cadence_evidence: IEA Myanmar natural-gas page is static explanatory country-profile content with no data vintage, no publication date and no stated refresh schedule; the only dates present are on unrelated linked reports.

reports.title: Myanmar–China merchandise trade statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from Chinese customs and related sources
reports.description: Bilateral trade with China. China is a dominant trade partner; Myanmar exports include ores, mineral fuels, rubber, copper and agricultural products; imports include vehicles, machinery, electrical equipment and fabrics. Border and informal flows are material.
reports._notes: Primary bilateral trade corridor under constrained official data.
reports._url_evidence: Myanmar Ministry of Commerce country-wise export/import/trade-volume table by fiscal year; China appears as entry 43 with FY2020-21 exports ~USD 5,179.73m and imports ~USD 4,646.21m. (China Customs' own bilateral bulletin at english.customs.gov.cn was also reachable but is not Myanmar-specific.)
reports._cadence_evidence: Ministry of Commerce country-wise trade page presents fiscal-year aggregates - FY2020-2021, FY2021-2022 (mini budget), FY2022-2023, FY2023-2024 and FY2024-2025 (April-June so far). One consolidated release per fiscal year; no monthly or weekly editions are listed.

reports.title: Poverty and living standards statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from World Bank-aligned and national monitoring sources
reports.description: Poverty rates and living-standards indicators. Poverty had declined substantially before 2021; subsequent conflict, economic contraction and displacement have reversed gains and elevated vulnerability, especially in conflict-affected areas.
reports._notes: Core welfare measurement node under elevated stress conditions.
reports._url_evidence: World Bank Myanmar Subnational Phone Surveys series page (8,500+ households across all 15 states/regions) listing 'Development Reversed: Poverty and Labor Markets in Myanmar' and the Sept 2025 poverty and labour markets report.
reports._cadence_evidence: World Bank Myanmar Subnational Phone Surveys page lists reports at irregular intervals - April 2023, May 2023, May 2024, September 2025, June 2026, plus a 2023-24 round technical note - and states no survey or publication frequency; the gaps are uneven, so no cadence can be counted.

reports.title: Exchange-rate regime and parallel-market statistics
reports.publisher: Central Bank of Myanmar / parallel-market trackers
reports.description: Official and parallel-market exchange rates for the kyat. Multiple rates and a persistent parallel-market premium are structural features under currency controls, limited FX availability and elevated inflation.
reports._notes: Critical price and external-constraint node. Parallel-market premium is a key signal.
reports._url_evidence: MMSIS 'Foreign Exchange Rates' indicator page showing the official monthly kyat rate against USD and EUR from Aug 2021 to Jul 2022 (1,684-1,850 kyat/USD). Official rate only - the parallel-market side of this item is not covered, and the CBM's own FX pages are unreachable via WebFetch.
reports._cadence_evidence: MMSIS foreign exchange rate indicator is a monthly series (kyat per USD and EUR) with one observation per month from 2021.08 to 2022.07. Series is dormant - the last period posted is July 2022 - but its cadence while running was monthly.

reports.title: Labour force and employment statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from ILO modelled estimates and national sources
reports.description: Labour-force participation, employment-to-population ratio and unemployment rates. Participation is in the low-60s percent range; unemployment is moderate by modelled estimates, but informal employment and underemployment are widespread and conflict has disrupted livelihoods.
reports._notes: Primary labour-market node under constrained survey conditions.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved and read: Myanmar Statistical Yearbook 2024, Part 2 (Central Statistical Organization), Chapter 7 'Labour and Employment' (pp.265-282). It carries labour-force participation rates by age group, the unemployment rate (3.69% in 2023), employment through the 91 Labour Exchange Offices (936,000+ registrations in 2023), overseas employment (219,701 in 2023-24), government/private employment splits by sex and by state/region, and social-security registrations, with series running 2010-2024. This is a national official product, replacing the ILOSTAT country profile that returns HTTP 403 to every fetch.
reports._url_route: national publisher instead of ILO - CSO publications index (csostat.gov.mm)
reports._cadence_evidence: The linked file is Myanmar Statistical Yearbook 2024 Part 2, an annual CSO volume; its labour tables are annual data points 2020-2023 drawn from the Labour Force Projection Report, while the underlying LFS itself is described as two semi-annual collection rounds (Jan-Mar and Sep-Nov). The publication counted here is the annual yearbook.

reports.title: Fiscal balance and budget deficit statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from World Bank-aligned and national fiscal monitoring
reports.description: Fiscal balance and deficit indicators. The deficit has widened in recent fiscal years (mid-single-digit percent of GDP range) under reconstruction, security and recurrent spending pressures, with weak tax collection and reliance on domestic financing including central-bank channels.
reports._notes: Core fiscal-flow node under constrained revenue and elevated spending pressures.
reports._url_evidence: World Bank Myanmar Economic Monitor series page - 'a biannual perspective on economic developments and key challenges in Myanmar', editions Oct 2013 through June 2026, covering the fiscal situation, financial sector and outlook.
reports._cadence_evidence: World Bank page states outright that 'The Myanmar Economic Monitor series provides a biannual perspective on economic developments', and the edition list confirms two per year - June and December 2023, 2024, 2025 and June 2026.

reports.title: Border trade statistics and framing
reports.publisher: Derived from Ministry of Commerce and monitoring sources
reports.description: Statistics and analytical framing of official and informal border trade, especially with China and Thailand. Border trade volumes have fluctuated sharply with conflict, checkpoint control and infrastructure disruption; informal and non-state-controlled flows remain material.
reports._notes: High-centrality trade densification under fragmented territorial control.
reports._url_evidence: Myanmar Ministry of Commerce table of actual export/import/trade volume by border station for FY2020-21 to FY2024-25, covering 16 stations including Muse, Myawaddy, Chinshwehaw and Kawthaung, in USD millions.
reports._cadence_evidence: Ministry of Commerce export-by-region page shows fiscal-year totals for 2020-21 through 2024-25 (latest covering April-June of the mini-budget period). The page notes the underlying customs data is weekly, but the published tables are compiled per fiscal year.

reports.title: Internal displacement and humanitarian needs statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from OCHA / UN Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan and monitoring sources
reports.description: Statistics on internal displacement and humanitarian needs. Internally displaced persons are in the multi-million range (approximately 3.7 million cited in recent monitoring); the 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan projects over 16 million people requiring assistance. Conflict, insecurity and disaster overlays drive large-scale vulnerability.
reports._notes: High-centrality humanitarian and social-stress node. Distinctive under current conditions.
reports._url_evidence: OCHA Myanmar Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026: 16.2 million people requiring life-saving assistance, ~3.6 million displaced by conflict and earthquake, 4.9 million targeted at USD 890 million.
reports._cadence_evidence: OCHA page is the Myanmar Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026, an annual planning instrument; the text benchmarks itself against the prior year's edition ($890 million requested, a 36 per cent decrease from the $1.4 billion requested in 2025). No explicit frequency statement, but one plan per calendar year.

reports.title: Rare earths and critical minerals production framing
reports.publisher: Derived from USGS and trade sources
reports.description: Framing of rare earths, tin, antimony and related critical-mineral production. Myanmar ranks among the world’s larger producers of rare earths, tin and antimony; much production is artisanal or outside full government control, with China the primary destination.
reports._notes: Critical-minerals densification complementing gas and jade.
reports._url_evidence: USGS National Minerals Information Center country page for Burma (Myanmar) with Minerals Yearbook chapters 1994-2022; states Burma was the world's 4th-ranked rare earths producer (7.1% of global output), 6th in tin (6.8%) and 5th in antimony (3.8%) in 2024.
reports._cadence_evidence: USGS Burma country page lists one Minerals Yearbook country chapter per year for 1994-2015, then 2016, a combined 2017-18, 2019 and a combined 2020-21, with data tables 2002-2021 plus a 2022 tables-only release. Nominally annual, though recent editions are combined and lag by several years; the page states no frequency in words.

reports.title: Education and learning outcomes framing
reports.publisher: Derived from World Bank, UNICEF and national monitoring sources
reports.description: Framing of education access and learning outcomes. Foundational literacy and numeracy were already weak pre-crisis (very high learning poverty); subsequent disruption has further eroded proficiency and participation.
reports._url_evidence: World Bank Myanmar Monitoring Platform education page describing analysis of trends and disparities in educational outcomes, linking 'Educational Access and Learning Outcomes in Myanmar' and out-of-school children reports.
reports._cadence_evidence: World Bank Myanmar education monitoring brief describes an ongoing study and monitoring effort, not a scheduled series. Only one dated output is shown (State of Education in Myanmar, July 2023) and no frequency is stated.
